slides.heading: range()
slides.body: range() is part of Definite Iteration. This short lesson gives you a practical Python idea you can understand, try, and reuse in simple programs.

slides.heading: Core Idea: range()
slides.body: range() produces a sequence of numbers for a for loop. You can choose a start, stop, and step.

slides.heading: Real-World Analogy
slides.body: range() is like a number dispenser that gives the next ticket number until it reaches the stop point.

annotations.note: This line starts a loop that processes each value in a sequence.
This line displays a value or message on the screen.

slides.heading: Key Rule
slides.body: Use for loops when you want to repeat through a known range or sequence.
